stem: A laboring client has a doula in addition to the RN and obstetric clinician. Which action by the RN best reflects appropriate collaboration with the doula?

options.A: Invite the doula to provide comfort measures, emotional support, and help the client communicate preferences while the RN continues clinical nursing care.
options.B: Ask the doula to independently interpret changes in the fetal heart rate tracing and recommend whether obstetric intervention is needed.
options.C: Delegate administration of a prescribed as-needed analgesic to the doula when the RN is caring for another client.
options.D: Require the doula to stop bedside labor support once the RN is present so that only one person provides continuous emotional support.

rationale: A is correct. Current ACOG guidance describes the doula's role as complementary to the medical team and identifies physical and emotional support, education, support for self-advocacy, communication of preferences, and labor comfort measures as appropriate doula functions. CMS likewise describes doula services as emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional. B is incorrect because independent fetal-monitor interpretation and recommendations for obstetric intervention are clinical functions, not nonclinical doula support. C is incorrect because medication administration is a clinical task and is outside the nonclinical doula role. D is incorrect because doula support is intended to complement clinical care; ACOG specifically recommends respectful clinician-doula teamwork rather than excluding the doula when clinical staff are present.
educational_objective: Collaborate with a doula as a nonclinical support professional who complements nursing and obstetric care by providing physical, emotional, educational, and communication support without assuming clinical assessment, treatment, or medication-administration functions.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists (ACOG); Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
source_document_title: Partnering With Doulas in Clinical Settings, Committee Statement No. 31; Transforming Maternal Health (TMaH) Model Frequently Asked Questions
source_version_date: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31, August 2026, published online July 16, 2026; CMS TMaH FAQ current page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31 — Background: doula work is complementary to the medical team; doulas support self-advocacy, provide physical and emotional support, help clients navigate medical decisions and communicate preferences, and provide education. Recommendations and Conclusions: create respectful teams that include doulas; continuous support includes comfort measures and reassurance. CMS TMaH Model FAQ, Question 20 'What doula care services will be covered in the TMaH Model?': doula services are emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional during pregnancy, delivery, and after childbirth.
source_claim_supported: Doulas are nonclinical support professionals whose role complements the clinical team through physical, emotional, educational, informational, advocacy, and communication support rather than clinical assessment or treatment.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, page 7; Related Activity Statements from the 2024 RN Practice Analysis include 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care' and 'Advocate for client rights and needs.'
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — appropriate collaboration with a nonclinical birth-support professional
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's definition-style item into a bedside collaboration scenario using newly current ACOG 2026 guidance and CMS's explicit nonclinical definition. Replaced implausible claims about replacing the nurse or holding overall medical authority with realistic boundary decisions involving fetal assessment, medication administration, and complementary bedside support.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: intrapartum support / doula-clinician collaboration / Management of Care
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against ACOG Committee Statement No. 31, the most current 2026 national obstetric guidance located for clinician-doula partnerships, and CMS's TMaH FAQ defining doula services as nonclinical emotional, physical, and informational support.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A uses functions explicitly described by ACOG and preserves the RN's clinical role. B requires clinical fetal assessment and treatment recommendation, inconsistent with a nonclinical support role. C assigns a clinical medication-administration function to a nonclinical doula. D contradicts ACOG's partnership model and the complementary nature of continuous doula support.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; reflects complementary physical, emotional, and communication support while nursing care continues.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect but plausible boundary error; fetal heart-rate interpretation and obstetric intervention recommendations are clinical functions.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect but plausible delegation error; prescribed medication administration is not part of nonclinical doula support.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect but plausible team-process error; the presence of an RN does not negate the doula's complementary continuous-support role.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A preserves both the source-supported doula functions and the clinical/nonclinical boundary. B and C cross that boundary; D unnecessarily removes a complementary support role.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are framed as concrete RN collaboration decisions in the same labor setting; the correct answer is not identifiable by length or a definitional restatement alone.
audit_findings.blueprint: The item tests collaboration and advocacy within the care-delivery team, directly aligned with Management of Care activity statements in the 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked ACOG's current role description, the complementary-team language, CMS's nonclinical definition, and each distractor for possible state-scope ambiguity. The final item avoids assigning a legally defined doula scope by state and instead relies on nationally described nonclinical doula support. No second answer or unresolved scope conflict remained.
